notes:
**A bot rule that blocks Google is no longer reported as an AI problem.**

Docket asks your own server for your homepage as each AI crawler and tells you
which ones it refuses. On a site whose firewall turns away *every* crawler that
identifies itself, that produced a report about AI visibility — while Googlebot
was being refused the same page, and the report never said so.

Docket now asks as Googlebot too, before it asks as anything else. When Google
is refused as well, the finding says plainly that this is not an AI-crawler
problem: a rule turning away self-identifying crawlers is turning away the
search engines, which costs far more, and it should be fixed as a crawler-access
problem rather than an AI one. Sites that block AI crawlers specifically read
exactly as they did before.

**A finding about analytics now names the tool it found.**

"Analytics is missing from 204 of 205 pages" sounds like a tag that was rolled
out badly. On the site that produced it, the only analytics-family tag anywhere
was a single Hotjar snippet on one page — there was no analytics deployment to
have gaps in. The finding now reads "Hotjar is missing from 204 of 205 pages"
and states that Hotjar appears on 1 page and no other analytics tag was found
anywhere, so you can see in one sentence what was actually measured.
